description: Macrolepiota procera, the Parasol Mushroom, is a large, choice edible mushroom with a tall stem bearing a distinctive snakeskin (brownish, banded) pattern and a movable double ring. It has a broad, scaly cap, white spore print, free gills, and no volva, and typically grows solitary or in groups in grassy clearings, pastures, and forest edges.
distribution: Widespread in temperate regions of Europe, North America, and Asia, and reported from other temperate areas worldwide.
edibilityNotes: A choice edible, but eat only the caps thoroughly cooked and discard the tough, fibrous stem; never eat raw. CRITICAL: confirm a white spore print and the complete absence of a volva before eating. The green-spored parasol (Chlorophyllum molybdites) is a common cause of serious gastrointestinal poisoning and has a GREEN spore print. More dangerously, young, unexpanded parasols can be confused with DEADLY Amanita species (e.g., the death cap and destroying angels), which have a VOLVA (cup or bulb at the stem base), often a smooth (non-snakeskin) stem, and may give a white spore print. Always check the stem base for a volva and take a spore print.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Chlorophyllum molybdites
dangerousLookalikes.note: Green-spored parasol; one of the most common causes of mushroom poisoning in North America (severe GI distress, not deadly). Distinguished by a GREEN spore print (vs. white in M. procera) and gills that age greenish; lacks the strongly snakeskin-banded stem. Always take a spore print.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Amanita species (young/button stage)
dangerousLookalikes.note: DEADLY Amanitas (death cap A. phalloides, destroying angels A. bisporigera/virosa) can resemble young unexpanded parasols. Amanitas have a VOLVA (membranous cup or bulb at the stem base) and a smooth (not snakeskin-patterned) stem. Always dig up the full stem base and check for a volva.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Chlorophyllum brunneum
dangerousLookalikes.note: Shaggy parasol relative with an abrupt-bulbous stem base and a typically single (not movable double) ring; can cause gastrointestinal upset in some people.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Chlorophyllum rhacodes
dangerousLookalikes.note: Shaggy parasol; flesh reddens/bruises when cut and the stem lacks the snakeskin banding of M. procera. Generally edible when cooked but causes GI upset in some individuals; confirm white spore print.
